comment: Rank 1 reads 'Inavolisib 9 mg PO QD + bevacizumab on INTRINSIC' and anchors it on INAVO120 PFS HR 0.43 (95% CI 0.32-0.59, mPFS 15.0 vs 7.3 mo, pmid:39476340). That trial is RoB2:Low for HR+/HER2- breast — for CRC it is cross-tumor extrapolation, full stop, and the dossier's own case_match flag says cross_tumor_only. INTRINSIC's PIK3CA-mut mCRC arm has not posted PFS or OS. The CRC fallback is Juric 2018 alpelisib phase 1a: 2 PRs in the CRC subset of a 134-patient PI3K-altered basket, which is anecdote-grade. RMC-6236 at rank 2 is worse: zero A59T clinical data, the flagship monotherapy basket NCT05379985 restricts to codons 12/13/61 on protocol-defined text, and the rationale rests on the Knox/Jiang Nature mechanism papers plus a 'highest-yield phone call' framing. Mechanism plausibility is not evidence. Ranking a cross-tumor breast HR and a mechanism-only RAS(ON) inhibitor as #1 and #2 above the ALASCCA RoB2:Low RCT signal inverts the evidence pyramid.

Aligned on the FOLFIRI-bev floor, the peri-op bevacizumab hold, and the PRODIGE 7 framing — those are right. The push-back is on rank 4 'Botensilimab + balstilimab as a 3L+ trial-route option on CCTG NCT07152821.' The conservative rationale cites Bullock 2024 Nat Med n=101 phase 1b at all-comer ORR 17% (95% CI 10-26) with the NLM subset at ORR 22% and mOS 20.9 mo. That is a post-hoc-defined responder phenotype within a single-arm phase 1b expansion, then a randomized phase 2 against monotherapy rather than against BSC or chemo. By strict RoB2 / ROBINS-I logic, the n=70 NLM subset is hypothesis-generating; CCTG NCT07152821 vs BSC is the registrational test and has not read out. At my evidence bar this should sit below the standard 2L/3L backbone (aflibercept-FOLFIRI VELOUR HR_OS 0.82; ramucirumab-FOLFIRI RAISE HR_OS 0.84; SUNLIGHT TAS-102+bev HR_OS 0.61; FRESCO-2 fruquintinib HR_OS 0.66; CORRECT/CONCUR regorafenib HR_OS 0.77/0.55), all of which have replicated phase 3 OS signal. Rank 4 reads too high.

The whole frame prioritizes effect-size potential over reproducibility, and the notes anchor on 'a 37yo whose mid-20s-month median OS on standard sequencing is the bar we are trying to beat.' That bar is wrong. For an MSS young patient with peritoneal-predominant disease and resected liver-only oligometastatic history, optimal sequencing on a fit 37-year-old is FOLFOXIRI+bev 1L (TRIBE2 mOS 27.4 vs 22.5, HR 0.82; TRIBE earlier readout 29.8 vs 25.8) into 2L oxaliplatin-or-irinotecan swap with anti-angiogenic continuation or aflibercept (VELOUR HR_OS 0.82) or ramucirumab (RAISE HR_OS 0.84) into 3L SUNLIGHT TAS-102+bev (HR_OS 0.61, mOS 10.8 vs 7.5 added to prior median) into 4L fruquintinib (FRESCO-2 HR_OS 0.66) or regorafenib. Stacked, that reaches the 28-32 mo range, not 21. Daraxonrasib for KRAS A59T at rank 1 has zero A59T clinical data; the NCT05379985 monotherapy basket excludes by codon-12/13/61 protocol text; RASolve-GI is a sponsor-confirmation gate. Effect-size potential without an A59T-specific readout is mechanism plausibility, not evidence. Recalibrate the SoC bar before ranking experimental switches above it.

Rank 5 bundles 'CAIRO6 (NCT02758951), INTRINSIC (NCT04929223), CCTG NCT07152821 bot/bal vs BSC, RASolve-GI (NCT06445062)' under the NCCN-endorses-trial-enrollment frame, and that frame quietly upgrades pre-readout single-arm and basket protocols to the same shelf as ALASCCA-grade RCT evidence. NCCN category 2A means lower-level evidence plus uniform expert consensus, and the historical record on 2A is mixed: IMblaze 370 (Eng 2019 Lancet Oncol, n=363, OS HR 1.00, 95% CI 0.73-1.38) put cobimetinib + atezolizumab through phase 3 and the MEK+ICI rationale died on a regimen that 2A-class consensus had endorsed pre-readout in MSS CRC. Same lesson on KEYNOTE-651, on porcupine inhibitors for APC-loss tumors, on PARPi+ICI in HRD-undefined CRC. The concensusite frame allows INTRINSIC PIK3CA-mut mCRC (no arm-specific PFS yet, cross-tumor anchor) and RMC-6236 RASolve-GI (sponsor-confirmation gated, no A59T clinical data) to ride at the same rank as ALASCCA RoB2:Low. Ranking those slots is fine; framing them as guideline-aligned-and-therefore-vetted is the overreach. Also: rank 4 carries ALASCCA into the metastatic peritoneal setting on a guideline-permitted-extrapolation flag, which is honest, but the NCCN v4.2025 PIK3CA-aspirin language lives in stage II-III adjuvant — calling it 'guideline-supported' for active stage IV disease compresses the indication gap.

Targeting rank-4 not rank-1 because inavolisib and RMC-6236 are where we mostly agree. The advocate's CRS-HIPEC framing reads PRODIGE 7 (pmid:33417845) as essentially closing oxaliplatin HIPEC but stops short of arguing mitomycin C HIPEC at a Sugarbaker-trained center still carries a defensible peritoneal-control signal for a 37yo. Van der Speeten's MMC peritoneal:plasma AUC ratio of 20-25x (pmid:20689948) is the pharmacokinetic argument PRODIGE 7 did not test, and at a young-patient high-volume center I would push harder for MMC HIPEC than the dossier-row hedging implies.

Ranking daraxonrasib at #5 'hypothetical until sponsor confirms' and bot/bal at #4 turns a 37yo's 28-32 month median OS into a sequencing exercise with mostly-known endpoints. The case is exactly the population where a single Revolution Medicines eligibility call (medinfo@revmed.com, NCT06445062) carries asymmetric upside; refusing to rank it ahead of FOLFOXIRI intensification is a posture choice masquerading as evidence rigor. The preference file is efficacy-leaning at 0.7 with trials-preferred and no veto, and 'surface all options' authorizes putting the A59T sponsor inquiry at rank 1-2 contingent on confirmation, not parking it below FOLFOX 2L as a hypothetical.

The critic's RoB2-only standards flagged bot/bal as 'informal:med, single-arm phase 1b plus randomized phase 2 vs monotherapy, no BSC comparator' — and that same threshold would have excluded the Bullock 2024 Nat Med (pmid:38871975) NLM signal from any 2025 board recommendation, despite being the clearest MSS-CRC ICI breakthrough in a decade. At what evidence threshold does the critic accept hypothesis-grade signals for a 37yo with rapidly fatal disease whose peritoneal-only phenotype maps onto the exact responder subset (ORR 22%, mOS 20.9 mo)? The CCTG phase 3 (nct:NCT07152821) reads out in 2027-2028; the patient does not get to wait.

NCCN Colon v1.2026 closes anti-EGFR on any-RAS-mutant and closes the G12C-selective drugs by allele, but the guideline text does not even mention KRAS A59T — it lags the biomarker biology by years. Arena 2021 (pmid:34031055) functionally characterized A59 alleles with lower MAPK output and 'occasional responders' to anti-EGFR, and the preference file's 'surface all options' framing with efficacy-weight 0.7 explicitly authorizes outside-guideline thinking when the biology supports it. Treating A59T as a flat anti-EGFR contraindication and closing the door on RMC-6236 / JAB-23E73 sponsor inquiries (nct:NCT06445062, nct:NCT06973564) on guideline-fit grounds is reading consensus into a gap NCCN has not addressed.

Ranking inavolisib + bev above the NCCN-endorsed 1L backbone is the load-bearing problem. NCCN Colon Cancer v1.2026 lists FOLFIRI + bev and FOLFOXIRI + bev at category 1 / category 2A preferred for 1L; ESMO mCRC (Cervantes 2023, Ann Oncol 34:10-32) carries the same backbone at level I, recommendation A, MCBS 3. PIK3CA-directed therapy in mCRC is nowhere in NCCN v1.2026 as a 1L option, and INAVO120 (NEJM 2024 pmid:39476340) is HR+/HER2- breast, not CRC. INTRINSIC is the trial slot, which is fine, but the trial slot is the guideline-aligned route at progression for the PIK3CA-mut cohort, not a 1L displacement of the category-1 chemo+bev backbone. The same critique applies to RMC-6236 at rank 2: guideline-level management of KRAS A59T at 1L is the standard chemo+bev backbone with no anti-EGFR, with trial enrollment as the guideline-aligned route when a biomarker-defined investigational option fits. The Arena 2021 functional data (pmid:34031055) argues that A59T should be assessed individually rather than as a flat anti-EGFR contraindication, which I agree with for a research framework, but the consensus seat reads RMC-6236 at 1L on an n=0 efficacy signal for the allele and a sponsor-confirmation contingency as outside the NCCN / ESMO endorsement.

Aligned with the conservative seat on the SoC floor and on the bev peri-op hold being non-negotiable. The qualifier is that NCCN Colon Cancer v1.2026 keeps FOLFOXIRI + bevacizumab at category 2A preferred 1L for fit patients, and ESMO mCRC (Cervantes 2023) grades it level I, recommendation A with MCBS 3 on the basis of TRIBE (Loupakis 2014 pmid:25337750, mPFS 12.1 vs 9.7 mo, HR 0.75) and TRIBE2 (Cremolini 2020 pmid:32007158, mOS 27.4 vs 22.5 mo, HR 0.82). A 37-year-old with peritoneal-predominant disease is exactly the TRIBE-eligible population, and the intensification conversation belongs on the table at 1L rather than waiting for FOLFIRI-bev progression. The conservative posture reads intensification as escalation; the guideline reads it as a permitted preferred option for fit patients. I would amend rank 1 to surface the FOLFOXIRI + bev upgrade explicitly, with the bev peri-op hold logic intact, the DPYD / UGT1A1 genotyping prerequisite intact, and an OPTIMOX stop-and-go schedule built in to manage cumulative oxaliplatin neuropathy for a young patient with a long runway.

Agreement on the PRODIGE 7 caveat and on the aspirin biomarker-match argument. Where the strict-evidence frame gets in the way is on three items the guidelines have already absorbed despite imperfect single-trial evidence. First, NCCN Colon Cancer v4.2025 formally adopted the ALASCCA recommendation (low-dose aspirin 100-162 mg PO QD for PIK3CA-mutant resected stage II-III CRC) on a single phase 3 with a Group A 95% CI upper bound at 0.98 — the consensus seat reads that as collective expert calibration of the same fragility the critic flags, not as a separate problem. The metastatic extrapolation gap is real and worth keeping in the rationale, but ranking aspirin as the most defensible single intervention is consistent with the NCCN read. Second, botensilimab + balstilimab in MSS CRC is single-arm phase 1b plus randomized phase 2 vs monotherapy, which the critic flags accurately, and which the guidelines acknowledge by listing the trial route as the preferred pathway pending CCTG NCT07152821 OS readout. The Bullock 2024 NLM phenotype match for this patient is the reason NCCN-endorsed access goes through the trial, not off-trial. Third, tumor-informed ctDNA MRD (Signatera class) is now in NCCN Colon Cancer v3.2024 / v1.2026 as a category 2A prognostic consideration on GALAXY-CIRCULATE-Japan (Kotani 2023 pmid:34754095) plus the IDEA / CALGB-SWOG-80702 secondary analyses, with Medicare coverage in stage II-IV CRC. RoB2 grade does not exclude it because the guideline already absorbed the imperfect evidence as a prognostic biomarker. The critic's strict-evidence pyramid is the right frame for off-label payer fights; the consensus seat reads it as too narrow for items the field has already calibrated.

Daraxonrasib at rank 1 on a sponsor-confirmation contingency sits outside the NCCN and ESMO consensus stack for this patient, and the framing that this is the biggest upside swing reads past the entire reason guidelines exist. NCCN Colon Cancer v1.2026 directs 1L management of KRAS-mutant mCRC to FOLFIRI + bev (category 1) or FOLFOXIRI + bev (category 2A preferred for fit patients), with anti-EGFR explicitly off the table for any non-wild-type RAS at exons 2/3/4; KRAS A59T sits in exon 3, so anti-EGFR is excluded at the guideline level on Sorich 2015 (pmid:25115304, n=5,948, OS HR 1.08 in new-RAS-mut) and Schirripa 2015 (pmid:24806288). ESMO mCRC 2023 carries the same exclusion at level I. RMC-6236 has no published clinical efficacy data in KRAS A59T at any line. The flagship monotherapy basket (NCT05379985) restricts to codons 12/13/61. RASolve-GI (NCT06445062) protocol text reads RAS-mutated CRC but sponsor-level operational definitions typically narrow to 12/13/61, which is why even the conservative seat names sponsor confirmation as the gating step. Knox / Jiang 2024 Nature (pmid:38778097, pmid:38778099) is preclinical RAS(ON) pan-allele mechanism plausibility, not A59T-specific evidence. Guidelines exist precisely to constrain enthusiasm for n=0 efficacy data on an allele, and ranking an off-protocol n=0 pick above the category-1 1L backbone is the move the consensus seat is built to push back on. The guideline-aligned route for this patient is the category-1 backbone now, the bev peri-op hold around CRS, the CRS at a high-volume center with HIPEC honestly framed per PRODIGE 7 (Quenet 2021 pmid:33417845), and trial enrollment on RASolve-GI as the access route once sponsor confirms A59T eligibility, not as the 1L pick before that confirmation lands.

target_intervention_label: Inavolisib 9 mg PO QD + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV Q3W on INTRINSIC (NCT04929223)
comment: Advocate rank 1 is 'Inavolisib 9 mg PO QD + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV Q3W on INTRINSIC (NCT04929223)' at confidence high, placed above the FOLFIRI+bev the patient is currently tolerating. That ranking does not survive the indication map. INAVO120 (Jhaveri 2024 NEJM, PFS HR 0.43, 95% CI 0.32-0.59, mPFS 15.0 vs 7.3 mo) is HR+/HER2- breast, not CRC. The INTRINSIC PIK3CA-mut CRC arm has no published arm-specific PFS or OS, and the CRC PI3K-alpha clinical floor is Juric 2018 alpelisib at 2 PRs across the n=134 CRC subset of a phase 1a basket. M1043I is exon 20 kinase-domain but non-canonical relative to H1047R / E545K / E542K, which is the dataset INAVO120 powered on. Putting this above FOLFIRI+bev needs a CRC-population PFS or OS readout the dossier does not contain. Same critique on RMC-6236 at rank 2: zero A59T clinical data, sponsor eligibility unconfirmed, and ranking it ahead of the proven 2L FOLFOX+bev backbone treats a phone call as a recommendation. Conservative read: inavolisib reserve for 2L on INTRINSIC routing after documented FOLFIRI+bev progression and after M1043I somatic / clonal confirmation; daraxonrasib stays hypothetical until Revolution Medicines confirms A59T eligibility.

target_intervention_label: Daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) on RASolve-GI (NCT06445062), contingent on sponsor accepting KRAS A59T
comment: Risktaker rank 1 is 'Daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) on RASolve-GI (NCT06445062), contingent on sponsor accepting KRAS A59T' at confidence low. The confidence label is honest; the rank is not. A single sponsor email decides whether the pick exists at all, the published RMC-6236 / RMC-7977 package carries no A59T in-vivo regression data, and the flagship monotherapy basket NCT05379985 restricts to codons 12/13/61 by protocol text. Putting a hypothetical intervention above the FOLFIRI+bev backbone the patient is currently tolerating inverts the evidence hierarchy the conservative floor exists to protect. Separate concern on rank 3, 'Botensilimab + balstilimab + fasting-mimicking diet + IV vitamin C, USC NCT06336902': this stacks G>=3 irAE around 35% (colitis 12%, hepatitis 8%) on top of a fasting-mimicking diet and IV vitamin C layer with no controlled signal, on a patient heading into CRS. The cumulative risk is real, the FMD + IV-C contribution to AE attribution is uncharacterized, and the risktaker's own primary_concerns row concedes 'no controlled signal'. Qualified on toxicity grounds: if bot/bal becomes relevant at 3L+, drop the FMD and IV vitamin C adjuncts unless the USC protocol mandates them and the team has a defined nutritional / volume management algorithm. Do not stack research-only adjuncts on top of an investigational ICI signal in an MSS patient with active peritoneal disease.

target_intervention_label: Low-dose aspirin 160 mg PO QD as post-CRS adjuvant-equivalent maintenance in the PIK3CA-pathway-altered patient, sequenced around the surgical bleeding window
comment: Largely aligned. Critic rank 1 is 'Low-dose aspirin 160 mg PO QD as post-CRS adjuvant-equivalent maintenance in the PIK3CA-pathway-altered patient', and the ALASCCA HR 0.49 (95% CI 0.24-0.98) plus the Yang/Meyerhardt 80702 celecoxib subset (DFS HR 0.56, OS HR 0.41) plus Liao 2012 (HR 0.18) concordance argument is the right read, with the adjuvant-vs-metastatic gap named honestly. Co-signing the PRODIGE 7 framing in the notes: CRS retains OS, oxaliplatin HIPEC does not, and the negative trifecta with COLOPEC and PROPHYLOCHIP is unambiguous. The push-back is on what the strict-evidence floor leaves off the board. The user asked for 'all options surfaced honestly', not just the highest-RoB2 tier. Three items the critic excluded that I would have ranked even with caveats: FOLFOXIRI + bev as a guideline-supported intensification conversation for a fit 37-year-old per TRIBE / TRIBE2 (mOS 27.4 vs 22.5 mo, HR 0.82), Signatera-class ctDNA MRD bracketing the CRS-HIPEC window per the NCCN 2024 ctDNA adoption, and an explicit recommendation-against block on G12C inhibitors / MOUNTAINEER / BEACON / single-agent ICI in MSS so the next round does not have to re-litigate four labels. Strict evidence is the floor. Refusing to rank anything above the floor leaves the team without the actionable surface the preference file asked for.

target_intervention_label: Recommendations AGAINST: single-agent ICI for MSS / TMB-low / PD-L1-neg disease; MOUNTAINEER tucatinib + trastuzumab (RAS-WT label fails on KRAS A59T); KRAS-G12C inhibitors sotorasib and adagrasib (allele mismatch); encorafenib + cetuximab BEACON label (no BRAF V600E plus anti-EGFR gate)
comment: Strong agreement on FOLFOXIRI + bev intensification for a fit 37-year-old (TRIBE2 mOS 27.4 vs 22.5 mo, HR 0.82), on Signatera-class ctDNA MRD bracketing the CRS-HIPEC window per NCCN v1.2026, and on ALASCCA-derived aspirin 160 mg with the adjuvant-vs-metastatic caveat. Push-back on the rank-6 'Recommendations AGAINST' block specifically on the anti-EGFR closure for KRAS A59T. The Sorich 2015 meta-analysis (n=5,948, OS HR 1.08, 95% CI 0.91-1.28) is the right population-level anchor and the default in 2026 should be to treat A59T as RAS-mutant for 1L anti-EGFR purposes. The framing 'closes BEACON ... and MOUNTAINEER' reads tighter than the underlying biology supports. Arena 2021 (PMID 34031055) characterized A59-class alleles as retaining partial residual EGFR pathway sensitivity in some cases, with lower MAPK output than canonical G12 mutants, and the Lochhead 2018 single-patient panitumumab + FOLFIRI PR exists. The atypical-KRAS literature is still evolving. Soften from 'closed' to 'default-avoid pending functional characterization, with anti-EGFR rechallenge under a research framework (ASCEND-CRC NCT07318389) defensible at later lines if a specific A59T functional argument is made'. Conservative posture still rules out 1L anti-EGFR here; the door for a structured research-framework attempt at progression should not be welded shut.

target_intervention_label: Inavolisib 9 mg PO QD + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV Q3W on INTRINSIC (NCT04929223), held in reserve for 2L after documented FOLFIRI-bev progression or completion of the peri-HIPEC backbone
comment: Reserve-for-2L is the wrong posture for this preference file. The patient set efficacy weight at 0.70, asked for trials surfaced, and wrote 'surface the full option space - standard of care, off-label rational combinations, clinical trials, and compassionate-use pathways.' INTRINSIC (NCT04929223) is the trial slot that maps PIK3CA M1043I to inavolisib + bev today, and parking it behind documented FOLFIRI-bev progression converts a biomarker-aligned 1L trial enrollment into a fallback. INAVO120 (pmid:39476340) is cross-tumor breast data — fair caveat — but the conservative seat also wants to ration RMC-6236 to 'hypothetical until sponsor confirms.' For a 37-year-old whose KRAS A59T sits in the gap that every G12C-selective drug excludes, the highest-leverage move on the file is the medinfo@revmed.com / NCT06445062 sponsor inquiry, not a posture that won't rank the pick until the answer comes back. The conservative position protects the SoC floor honestly; it under-serves a preference set that explicitly asked for the experimental ceiling.

target_intervention_label: Inavolisib + bevacizumab on INTRINSIC (NCT04929223), PIK3CA cohort
comment: Aligned on the rank-1 RMC-6236 sponsor-call framing — that is the highest-yield single inquiry on the case and the risktaker reads it correctly. The qualified note is on the inavolisib pick at rank 2 with confidence low. M1043I is a recurrent kinase-domain activating allele and Vasan 2019 (pmid:31699932) tagged it as one of the sensitizing positions for PI3K-alpha-selective inhibition; INAVO120 PFS HR 0.43 (pmid:39476340) is cross-tumor, agreed, but INTRINSIC routes PIK3CA-mut mCRC directly to inavolisib + bev and keeps the bev backbone the patient already tolerates. The risktaker's own concern row flags KRAS A59T co-activation as a potential blunter of single-pathway PI3K-alpha response, which is the honest read, but confidence low under-sells the mechanism match for an efficacy-0.70 preference file. I would carry this at moderate, not low. Same direction, slightly higher conviction.

target_intervention_label: Inavolisib + bevacizumab on INTRINSIC NCT04929223 PIK3CA-mut arm, contingent on M1043I confirmation and arm-specific PFS readout before commitment
comment: The critic only ranked three picks and explicitly excluded RMC-6236, daraxonrasib, anti-EGFR consideration, and the entire BCL-xL / ATR axis on RoB2 grounds. The preference file does not say 'only OS-validated phase 3 options.' It says 'surface the full option space - standard of care, off-label rational combinations, clinical trials, and compassionate-use pathways.' The critic's notes section flags PRODIGE 7, the negative HIPEC trifecta, IMblaze 370, eprenetapopt closure, the Sorich 2015 anti-EGFR meta-analysis, navitoclax discontinuation, and ST316 abstract-only status — all of which I agree with — but those are exclusions, not picks. A 37-year-old with KRAS A59T at a sponsor-inquiry-confirmable trial slot (NCT06445062) needs that slot named even if confidence is low, because the alternative is sequencing through SoC stacks while a possibly-eligible RAS(ON) program runs without her. Strict RoB2 is the right tool for excluding bad picks. It is the wrong tool for honoring a 'surface all options' preference. The aspirin pick at rank 1 is correct; the refusal to rank a fourth or fifth slot fails the user's stated request.

target_intervention_label: Trial enrollment as the guideline-aligned route for biomarker-defined off-label options: CAIRO6 (NCT02758951) for the HIPEC window; INTRINSIC (NCT04929223) for PIK3CA at progression; CCTG NCT07152821 bot/bal vs BSC for MSS at 3L+; RASolve-GI (NCT06445062) RMC-6236 for the KRAS A59T sponsor inquiry
comment: Largely aligned on bundling the four biomarker-defined trials at rank 5, and the framing that trial enrollment is the guideline-permitted route for off-label biomarker hits is right. The push-back is on the timing logic. The concensusite seat treats INTRINSIC, CCTG NCT07152821, and RASolve-GI as 2L/3L+ slots that activate after progression. NCCN Colon Cancer v1.2026 does not prohibit 1L trial enrollment for biomarker-matched options — it endorses it — and the preference file asks for trials to be surfaced, which carries a stronger 'enroll now where possible' reading than 'park for progression.' INTRINSIC's PIK3CA-mut arm enrolls patients with PIK3CA-altered mCRC and the eligibility text does not gate to second-line. RASolve-GI sponsor confirmation is the gating step for KRAS A59T eligibility, not a line-of-therapy criterion. The concensusite frame is correct that 'recommendation-against' calls (G12C-selective drugs, MOUNTAINEER, BEACON, single-agent ICI) close cleanly at the guideline level. The frame is too cautious on whether biomarker-matched trials at 1L are guideline-aligned today. They are.
